Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only parses and reads the PKGBUILD file. During this operation, the package's lifecycle functions (pkgver(), prepare(), build(), package()) are NOT invoked — only the source variable is evaluated as a reference to the git repository. There are no top-level command substitutions, no external downloads, and no code execution of the package's internal logic. The file contains only standard AUR packaging constructs: a source definition pointing to a git repository (with md5sum=SKIP, which is normal for VCS sources), and a package() function that performs installation steps. Since none of these functions run during `--printsrcinfo`, there is no opportunity for malicious code execution through this gate alone. The SKIP checksum is explicitly permitted per the guidelines for VCS sources and does not constitute a security issue.
</details>
<evidence></even though the file contains a source reference to a git URL, this is a declarative variable assignment, not executable code. The actual execution of the package's build steps occurs later during `makepkg` without arguments, outside the scope of `--printsrcinfo`. The mkpath --printsrcinfo command only reads the PKGBUILD text and extracts its source information, without invoking any of the package's lifecycle functions.
</evidence>
<summary>The PKGBUILD is safe for `makepkg --printsrcinfo` because it only defines a source variable and does not execute any of its package functions.</summary>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The .SRCINFO file appears to be a standard AUR package metadata file. It declares a Python/PyQt6 application called LlamaTray for managing Llama.cpp models. The package uses git to fetch source code from the legitimate GitHub repository (https://github.com/DolbyDAX2/LlamaTray.git), has appropriate dependencies (python, python-pyqt6, python-psutil, python-requests), and includes an optional dependency for NVIDIA GPU monitoring. The md5sums is set to SKIP, which is standard practice for VCS sources. There are no suspicious network requests, obfuscated code, or unexpected file operations that would indicate a supply chain attack. The package metadata is consistent with the stated purpose of a Llama.cpp tray manager.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard AUR package metadata with no malicious indicators</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches the declared project repository at build time and installs its contents under `${pkgdir}/opt/LlamaTray`, which is consistent with packaging the stated application. It creates a launcher, desktop entry, and icons; no unrelated network request, code download, encoded or obfuscated command, credential theft, or data exfiltration is present.

The `killall -9 llama-server` cleanup in the wrapper is application-level process management and does not indicate a supply-chain attack. The mutable Git source and `SKIP` checksum are normal for a `-git` package and are hygiene considerations only, not evidence of malicious behavior.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard packaging with no malicious behavior detected</summary>
</security_assessment>
